name: Toyota
overview: Australia's perpetual market leader and automotive titan. Toyota began Australian operations in 1958 with LandCruisers on the Snowy Mountains Scheme and assembled vehicles locally at Port Melbourne and Altona from 1963 to 2017.
australian_history:
Toyota's Australian story began in 1958 when civil engineering contractor Leslie Thiess imported 13 FJ25 LandCruisers for use on the rugged construction terrain of the Snowy Mountains Hydro-Electric Scheme. Impressed by their unbreakable mechanical toughness, Thiess secured Queensland distribution rights in 1959, forming Thiess Toyota.

In 1963, Australian Motor Industries (AMI) at Port Melbourne, Victoria negotiated CKD (Complete Knock Down) assembly rights for Toyota passenger cars, making Australia Toyota's very first vehicle manufacturing site outside of Japan. The first vehicle assembled was the Tiara (RT20/RT30), quickly followed by the Corona in 1964, the Crown luxury sedan, and the Corolla (KE10) in 1968.

By the 1970s, Toyota had expanded into full Australian manufacturing. Toyota Motor Corporation Japan gradually acquired shares in AMI, renaming the operation Toyota Motor Corporation Australia (TMCA). Under the Federal Government's Button Car Plan in 1989, Toyota and General Motors-Holden established the United Australian Automotive Industries (UAAI) joint venture. Holden built the Commodore for Toyota to sell as the Toyota Lexcen, while Toyota manufactured the Corolla and Camry for Holden to sell as the Holden Nova and Apollo.

In 1994, Toyota commissioned a brand new, world-class vehicle manufacturing complex at Altona in Melbourne's western suburbs, transitioning Port Melbourne to engine manufacturing and casting. In 2000, Toyota introduced the Altona-built Avalon large sedan, later replaced in 2006 by the 3.5L V6 Aurion alongside the Camry. In 2010, Altona launched Australia's very first locally manufactured hybrid passenger car, the Camry Hybrid (AHV40), unveiled by Prime Minister Kevin Rudd.

Toyota officially overtook Holden and Ford in 2003 to become Australia's overall best-selling automotive brand, a crown it has held without interruption for over two decades. The HiLux utility and RAV4 crossover have repeatedly been Australia's #1 selling individual vehicles. Local car assembly concluded at Altona on October 3, 2017 after 54 years and 3,451,115 vehicles built. Toyota maintains its Australian headquarters, national engineering center, product design studio, and extensive testing grounds at Altona and Anglesea.

models_catalog.name: Tiara
models_catalog.overview: The first Toyota assembled in Australia by AMI in Port Melbourne, laying the foundation for Toyota's domestic manufacturing history.

generations.summary: 1.5L and 1.9L pushrod 4-cylinder engine, 3-speed manual, CKD assembly at Port Melbourne.

models_catalog.name: Corona
models_catalog.overview: Long-running Australian family car assembled in Port Melbourne across multiple generations until succeeded by the Camry.

generations.summary: Shovel-nose design, 1.5L 2R engine, established Toyota's reputation for build quality.
1.6L 12R engine, improved passenger comfort and local suspension tuning.
1.8L 16R and 2.0L 18R engines, popular company fleet and family vehicle.
Square-edged styling, Holden 1.9L Starfire 4-cylinder fitted to meet local content rules, also 2.0L 18R-C.
Last RWD Corona in Australia, 2.4L 22R-E EFI engine on Avante, IRS rear suspension.

models_catalog.name: Crown
models_catalog.overview: Toyota's flagship executive sedan and wagon, assembled locally by AMI until 1980 and then fully imported until 1991.

generations.summary: First Crown in Australia, 1.9L 3R engine, durable body-on-frame chassis.
2.0L M-series inline-6 introduced, Port Melbourne assembly.
Distinctive avant-garde body, 2.3L and 2.6L inline-6 engines.
Royal Lounge trim, 2.6L 4M engine, 4-speed automatic options.
2.8L 5M-E fuel-injected engine, digital instruments, imported from Japan.
Royal Saloon with 2.8L DOHC 5M-GE, TEMS electronic suspension.
Final Australian-market Crown, 3.0L 7M-GE inline-6, succeeded by Lexus LS400.

1.8L 2ZR-FE Dual VVT-i 100kW, Ascent, Conquest, Levin SX, and Levin ZR.
Sharp wedge styling; introduced Corolla Hybrid in 2016 pairing 1.8L with electric motor.
TNGA-C platform, 2.0L M20A-FKS petrol, 1.8L Hybrid, and AWD GR Corolla 221kW turbo.

models_catalog.name: Camry

2.4L 2AZ-FE VVTi and 3.0L 1MZ-FE V6; Altise, Ateva, Sportivo, and Azura grades.

Hybrid-only range featuring 5th-gen Toyota Hybrid System with 2.5L 4-cylinder.
